chapter: Back in Houston, Club Ebony and Boo Pleasant
title: Hiring pianist Boo Pleasant from San Antonio
summary: Cobb tells how he heard Boo Pleasant play in San Antonio, auditioned her in Houston, and brought her to Chicago where she stayed two years and drew men to the club.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Is that when you had Boo Pleasant with you?
What?
Is that when you had Boo Pleasant?
No, Boo was working with me out of Universal.
Oh, she was then. Oh, I'd never heard of her [before.]

Well, I brought her out of San Antonio, Texas. She joined me in -- I heard her in San Antonio at the Lakewood Country Club there, Johnny Phillips' place there. And she and Cecil Scott, the saxophone player that used to be with Bill Doggett that played 'Honky Tonk.'
Scotty Clifford.
Yeah, Clifford.
MR. : Clifford Scott.

Yeah, that's one -- you call him Scotty. And he came over. Bubba Bright -- and Boo was working with them. And Boo sat on the piano and (inaudible) for Christ sakes, she sounded like a man playing the piano. She ain't jiving. So I asked about (inaudible), said "I'd like to bring you to Houston while I'm down there and -- in a rehearsal and test your reading ability, and see if you can handle the book, if you enjoy the book or what." She said (inaudible). Yes. So I sent her a bus ticket to come to Houston. She come in and we rehearsed together at the El Dorado at a Ballroom, and she did a good job. I said, "Okay, send her back to San Antone." And I gave her a date to join me in Chicago at the Regal Theater, and I said, "I'll send you your air fare there."

And they all told her (inaudible). All of them said. "He that. They ain't going to do nothing." You know, "They all say that." And I sent it to her air mail special registered, and she had to sign for it. She stood up for it. And they all in the neighborhood, she says, "I got it, I got it, I got it." (Inaudible).

She met me in Chicago, but she had talked with my wife about her five year old daughter. She had a son too. My wife (inaudible) take care of her because she loved kids. (Inaudible) and she brought [P_________] with her, and my
wife just fell in love with her and took care of her, and Boo stayed with me two years. And we kept -- and the son finally come, and we kept him too, Ollie.
How old was Boo then, her late '20s or early '30s?
No, she wasn't 20 yet.
She wasn't?
No, no. No, no, she was about 19.
What did she look like, her looks? Was she pretty?
Beautiful, beautiful girl.
Really.
And all -- she was an asset to my blue group, 'cause the men come to watch her shake herself up on the piano and play.
Well, what's happened to Boo then?
